title: The Water Cycle
seo_title: Year 4 Science: The Water Cycle Worksheets (Evaporation and Condensation)
standard_text: Identify the part played by evaporation and condensation in the water cycle and associate the rate of evaporation with temperature.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection, and investigations into how temperature and wind affect evaporation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The Sun drives the water cycle; warmer water evaporates faster.
body_html:
How to think about it

The same water moves round and round the water cycle, powered by the Sun.

  • Evaporation: the Sun heats water and it becomes water vapour. Condensation: vapour cools into droplets that form clouds.
  • Precipitation: rain, sleet, snow or hail falls. Collection: water gathers in rivers, lakes, seas and underground.
  • Water evaporates faster when it is warmer, windier and spread out more.
Example

A puddle disappears on a hot day. Stage?

Liquid → gas

Answer: evaporation

Example

Dish: 100 ml at start, 45 ml left. Evaporated?

100 − 45

Answer: 55 ml

Common mistakes

  • Thinking clouds are water vapour gas (they are droplets).
  • Thinking water must boil to evaporate.
  • Thinking the water cycle makes new water.

faq.q: What are the stages of the water cycle?
faq.a: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection. Then the cycle starts again.

faq.q: What is the difference between evaporation and condensation?
faq.a: Evaporation is a liquid turning into a gas. Condensation is a gas cooling and turning back into a liquid.
Higher temperatures, wind and a bigger surface area all make water evaporate faster.

What is precipitation?
c: water falling from clouds as rain, sleet, snow or hail

items.q: What happens during collection in the water cycle?
c: Water vapour rises, cools and turns into tiny droplets that form clouds.
The Sun warms water in seas, lakes and puddles, and it turns into water vapour.
Droplets join together and fall as rain, sleet, snow or hail.
Water runs into rivers, lakes, the sea and underground, and collects there.

items.q: Why does a cold drink can get wet on the outside?
c: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold surface.

items.q: Which stage of the water cycle is this? Water runs into rivers, lakes, the sea and underground, and collects there.

What are clouds made of?
c: tiny droplets of water (or ice crystals)

items.q: Does water have to boil to evaporate?
c: No. It evaporates at any temperature, just faster when warm.

items.q: Does the water cycle make new water?
c: No. The same water moves round and round.
items.e: The water on Earth is reused.
